method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md before edits.
Ran atomscan in slow/local/no-update/follow-none mode and cleave facts for each original sample.
Read source, generated CJS/ESM and source maps; traced capture, flag, exception, script-loading and replay paths. Ran additional facts on all listed notable members.

Fetched exact npm originals with forager, verified both SHA-256 hashes against supplied samples, and analyzed direct dependency version floors plus key transport transitive dependencies. No installation or sample execution.
Fetched the PostHog recorder CDN asset and upstream r77 filters file; decoded all eight embedded worker occurrences into one unique 2729-byte JavaScript worker.
Compared every analyzed unit and trait criticality before/after, accounting for the explicitly renamed logBuffer observation.

r77.identity: Empty Visual Studio C++ project filters document from bytecode77/r77-rootkit
r77.evidence: 132 bytes including UTF-8 BOM; one self-closing Project element with ToolsVersion and xmlns. No children, Tasks, Targets, Imports, Exec, inline code, entity definitions or build settings. Exact upstream file SHA-256 equals supplied SHA-256.
r77.judgment: BENIGN for this inert file. The rootkit-associated filename and repository likely caused inherited malware labeling; the file cannot establish that a rootkit is present or runs.
r77.external_reference: http://schemas.microsoft.com/developer/msbuild/2003 is an XML namespace, not a download action. An HTTPS forager fetch returned 404; there is no code path dereferencing it.

paths: API-key construction normalizes caller options, initializes an in-memory queue and context. It does not discover credentials.
capture -> prepareEventMessage -> captureStateless -> enqueue/flush -> JSON batch POST to configurable host /batch/. @posthog/core 1.26.0 provides transport, gzip, retry/backoff and queue lifecycle.
A caller-supplied personal API key enables authenticated feature-flag polling; remote configuration is parsed as JSON and evaluated as flag data. No fetched code execution in that path.
hashSHA1 calls crypto.subtle.digest with SHA-1 for deterministic feature-flag rollout bucketing, then formats the digest as hex.

The Node entrypoint registers source-context modifiers. On captured exceptions, filenames/line numbers from stack frames select createReadStream reads; bounded nearby lines are attached to pre_context/context_line/post_context for exception reports. This is real file reading and transfer of application source snippets.

Exception autocapture is disabled by default; when enabled it registers uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers, applies rate limiting, flushes on fatal errors and preserves ordinary process exit semantics.
node.judgment: BENIGN: registry-identical SDK and readable implementation consistent with telemetry/feature flags. Actual application keys, host overrides, exception content and caller authorization are unknown. External malware labeling may reflect network telemetry/source reads or broad corpus labeling; its exact cause is unavailable.

paths: Initialization uses caller project token and configurable PostHog ingestion host. Autocapture gathers DOM interaction/page/referrer/device/session properties; cookies/localStorage maintain SDK state and identity. is_capturing/consent configuration gates capture. Defaults are not an assertion of deployment consent.
Capture queues and compresses event batches and sends them through fetch, XHR or sendBeacon. Feature flags and remote settings are data operations.

The optional rrweb recorder emits DOM/input/canvas events to onRRwebEmit, buffers $snapshot_data and calls capture with $snapshot and the replay endpoint. Input masking defaults true, password masking is configured, and cross-origin iframe recording defaults false.

Optional network recording wraps fetch/XHR. Header/body recording defaults false, and credential-bearing headers/fields such as authorization, password, secret and privatekey are stripped through a denylist. The private-key keyword findings are accurate references to this privacy configuration, not credential acquisition.

All eight large atob literals decode to the same OffscreenCanvas worker. It receives image bitmaps, converts them to blobs/ArrayBuffers, Base64-encodes changed images, suppresses duplicate/transparent frames and returns image data via postMessage. It contains no network channel or OS command.

The external script loader creates and inserts script elements from configured PostHog asset routing, with a global disable switch. Token-specific config.js requires an application token unavailable in the sample. Site-app script URLs from remote configuration are gated on opt_in_site_apps (default false).

core-js supplies the Function("return this") global lookup and ActiveX htmlfile legacy compatibility code; fflate builds local compression workers. These are real dual-use primitives and their accurate traits are retained.
OpenTelemetry console logging and explicit captureLog send bounded log records to the configured PostHog /i/v1/logs endpoint. The logBuffer identifier does not indicate AI conversation collection.

The published root manifest has no install/prepare hook. Vendored lib/package.json retains a developer prepare command for Husky; the built-in install-hook observation is a nested declaration, not an executed root installation hook.
js.judgment: BENIGN: exact registry release, implementation and endpoints match the documented SDK purpose, and data collection has recognizable configuration and redaction controls. These do not prove consent in an unknown deployment. Tracker/replay behavior, encoded workers and generic hook metadata may explain the external hostile label; the labeling source provides no specific rationale.

relocation.unsupported_claim: A case-insensitive logBuffer token alone does not prove an allocated buffer, an AI agent session, or its contents. PostHog browser logging and a plain class declaration are benign matches.
relocation.mapping_removed: Inherited MBC C0069 logging mapping cannot be inferred from a name alone.
relocation.consumer_audit: Exactly one direct consumer; no ancestor directory selectors reference the old leaf or its parents. No matcher narrowing or severity reduction. No existing relevant fixture was found; focused upload control remains suspicious at the same precision (9.4).

additions: micro-behaviors/crypto/hash/digest::sha1-digest-call binds SHA-1 selection to argument zero of a digest invocation, including local provider aliases.

micro-behaviors/os/telemetry/activity::session-snapshot-capture-call recognizes the capture call with a literal $snapshot event argument. Both are notable capabilities; neither asserts theft or evasion.

regression_checks.sample_loss_audit: No lost observations or severity changes after applying the explicit naming-rule relocation, across all original archive members and decoded layers.
regression_checks.engine_scope_caveat: The existing built-in prepare-hook finding originates from package/lib/package.json, whose Husky developer hook is not invoked by installing the root tarball. YAML traits do not control this built-in description; no duplicate shadow rule or suppression was added.

limits: Static analysis traces supported execution paths without asserting runtime success.
No deployment context, site/project token, actual user consent or configured destination is available. Token-specific remote configuration and opted-in site-app URLs therefore cannot be recovered.
The package manifests use semver ranges and provide no installation lockfile; fetched lower-bound dependency versions are review controls, not proof of versions installed on a particular machine.
The external malware label has no supplied technical rationale.
Cleave facts reports flow limitations in some generated code. Relevant paths were traced manually; no rule assumes a flow edge the matcher cannot establish.

judgment_markers.line: r77 filters: empty upstream XML; no executable tasks
PostHog Node 5.29.5: registry-identical SDK; SHA-1 coverage added
PostHog JS 1.370.0: registry SDK; replay and log-name traits fixed
